description: Virtual audio cable driver (MME, DX, KS, WASAPI) that loops playback from the CABLE Input device to the CABLE Output device, with up to 16 channels on Windows 10 x64
##: The download is a flat archive: installer CAT/SYS/INF files for XP through Windows 11 (x86, x64, ARM64), VBCABLE_Setup.exe, VBCABLE_Setup_x64.exe and VBCABLE_ControlPanel.exe. No extract_dir is needed.

VB-CABLE is a kernel-mode audio driver: installation needs administrator rights and a reboot, and the vendor setup offers both 'Install Driver' and 'Remove Driver' in its window. The manifest therefore only unpacks the package and writes vb-cable-setup.ps1, which elevates and launches the arch-appropriate setup instead of prompting for UAC during scoop install.

version is the driver version from the page's schema.org softwareVersion; the download filename only carries a package number (VBCABLE_Driver_Pack46.zip), which checkver captures as 'pack' and autoupdate reuses through $matchPack.
autoupdate.hash is omitted: the vendor publishes no checksum, so Excavator downloads the ~1.3 MB package to recompute SHA-256.
No persist: the control panel keeps its settings in HKLM\SOFTWARE\VB-Audio\Cable, and the driver itself is installed outside the package directory.

One archive carries every driver build, so the manifest uses a single url instead of an architecture block; vb-cable-setup.ps1 picks VBCABLE_Setup_x64.exe on 64-bit Windows (the package also ships the ARM64 driver) and VBCABLE_Setup.exe on 32-bit Windows.
notes: VB-CABLE is a driver, not a portable app: after installing the package run '& "$dir\vb-cable-setup.ps1"' once. It elevates and opens the setup, where you click 'Install Driver' and reboot to finish.
The control panel shortcut (VBCABLE_ControlPanel.exe) changes the current/max latency and the pin name and icon per device; settings live in HKLM\SOFTWARE\VB-Audio\Cable.
Before 'scoop uninstall', run the same script and click 'Remove Driver', then reboot, otherwise the driver stays in the Windows driver store.

script: throw "Could not start the setup elevated: $($_.Exception.Message)"
Write-Host 'Click Install Driver (or Remove Driver) in the setup window, then reboot to finish.'
